{{Short description|Crop scientist professor}}
'''Carol M. Duffus''' [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]]''',''' DIC''',''' [[Royal Society of Arts|FRSA]]''',''' [[Fellowship of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|FRSE]] is a British professor  who specialised in [[Agricultural science|crop science]] and [[Agricultural technology|technology]]. She worked in the [[Scotland's Rural College]] (SRUC) at [[King's Buildings]], Edinburgh, when in 1995, she was made a [[Fellowship of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]].

Duffus was first female president of the [[Association of Applied Biologists]], and wrote  a cameo piece ''The Influence of the Association on Public Opinion'' in the centenary newsletter, about the (lack) of opportunity to use the influence of biological scientists on UK government policy development, whilst recognising that some consultations during her tenure, have penetrated, though not perhaps into the wider public eye.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Association of Applied Biologists 1904-2004: A Celebration of Achievement. |date=2004 |publisher=Association of Applied Bioscientists |editor-last=Langton |editor-first=F. Allen |pages=26 |language=en |editor-last2=Thompson |editor-first2=Alwyn R. |editor-last3=Millman |editor-first3=Carol A.}}</ref>

Her research interests have include [[Plant growth analysis|plant growth]] regulation and growth biochemistry in [[cereal]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nutbeam |first1=Anthony R. |last2=Duffus |first2=Carol M. |date=1976-06-21 |title=Evidence for C4 photosynthesis in barley pericarp tissue |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0006-291X%2876%2991029-9 |journal=Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications |volume=70 |issue=4 |pages=1198–1203 |doi=10.1016/0006-291X(76)91029-9 |pmid=942441 |issn=0006-291X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> including her doctoral thesis on [[carbohydrate synthesis]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Duffus |first=Carol Margaret |date=1982 |title=Cereal grain biochemistry and related studies |url=https://era.ed.ac.uk/handle/1842/31452 |journal=University of Edinburgh Doctoral Thesis |language=en}}</ref>

She co-authored a book on seeds (1980),<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Duffus |first1=C. M. |title=Seeds and their uses |last2=Slaughter |first2=J. C. |date=1980 |publisher=J. Wiley |isbn=978-0-471-27798-9 |location=Chichester [Eng.]; New York}}</ref> and co-edited another on toxic substances in crop plants (1991),<ref>{{Cite book |title=Toxic substances in crop plants |date=1991 |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry |isbn=978-0-85186-863-9 |editor-last=D'Mello |editor-first=J. P. Felix |location=Cambridge |editor-last2=Duffus |editor-first2=C. M. |editor-last3=Duffus |editor-first3=J. H. |editor-last4=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref> as well as monographs on carbohydrate synthesis (1984,1986).<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Duffus |first1=C. M. |title=Carbohydrate metabolism in plants |last2=Duffus |first2=John H. |date=1984 |publisher=Longman |isbn=978-0-582-44642-7 |location=London}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Duffus |first=C.M. |title=Carbohydrate Synthesis And Degradation |date=1 May 1986 |publisher=John Wiley and Sons Inc. |isbn=9780470204702 |language=en}}</ref>

Her work has included research on [[amyloplast]]s<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Williams |first1=J. Margaret |last2=Duffus |first2=Carol M. |date=1977 |title=Separation and Some Properties of Large and Small Amyloplasts throughout Development in Barley Endosperm
